name: KEI Industries Ltd
title: KEI Industries Ltd - 517569 - Transcript Of Analysts/Investors Call Pertaining To The Audited Financial Results For The Quarter And Year Ended On March 31, 2026.

summary.headline: KEI Q4 FY26 net sales rose 19.3% to INR3,476 crores and PAT 25.5% to INR284 crores; management guides 17-18% FY27 volume growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales were INR3,476 crores (up about 19.3%), with EBITDA margin of 12.21% (vs 11.6%) and PAT of INR284.31 crores (up 25.5%, margin 8.18%). For FY26, net sales reached INR11,746 crores (up 20.66%), EBITDA INR1,387 crores (11.81% margin) and PAT INR918 crores. Q4 volume growth was only about 2%, which management attributed to capacity constraints, with Sanand plant sales under INR100 crores in the quarter. Middle East shipping disruption in March cost an estimated INR50-60 crores of exports, and April freight costs are being shared with customers.

segments.name: Domestic institutional cables (FY26)
segments.commentary: Institutional cable sales INR2,688 crores; EHV domestic institutional sales INR559 crores vs INR308 crores (up 82%). Institutional share 42% of total, flat YoY.

segments.name: Exports (FY26)
segments.commentary: Export sales INR1,833 crores vs INR1,267 crores (up 45%). Q4 exports INR443 crores. Main markets Middle East, Australia, Africa, US and Europe; US order book about INR50-60 crores at 31 March 2026.

segments.name: Dealer distribution (FY26)
segments.commentary: Distribution sales INR6,349 crores, up 25%, 54% of sales. About 2,125 active dealers; around 10-12% dealer churn annually.

segments.name: EPC (non-cable) (FY26)
segments.commentary: EPC sales INR311 crores vs INR343 crores (about 2.6% of revenue). Q4 EPC INR123 crores vs INR72 crores, of which EHV EPC INR106 crores. Management targets 2-3% share over time.

segments.name: Stainless steel wire (FY26)
segments.commentary: Sales INR212 crores, flat YoY; Q4 INR55 crores vs INR46 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at 17-18% (company-wide), driven by Chinchpada wire capacity and the Sanand cable plant; management says value growth should exceed 20% at current metal prices.
FY28 volume growth expected at about 17-18% from Sanand phase 2, with overall revenue growth around 20% (management said it could be about 20%).
FY27 EBITDA margin guided conservatively at 10.5-11%; management expects roughly 20-25 bps annual improvement from scale, and about 0.5% extra from Sanand full capacity in FY28.
Export share targeted at about 20% of total sales in FY27, with US exports restarting; management aims for about INR40 crores per month US sales within about 3 months.
Capex of INR600-700 crores per year for the next 2-3 years, funded from internal accruals; company to stay debt-free for the next 4-5 years.
Net working capital days expected to ease; receivable days to fall from 1.88 months to about 1.75 months, and inventory+debtors-creditors from 3.39 to 2.97 months (already achieved).
capex_capacity: Sanand plant phase 1 commissioned in December 2025 after a 6-month delay; phase 2 (EHV) now expected by March 2027.
Chinchpada plant wire capacity added in Q2 FY25 and drives FY27 wire volume growth; Rajasthan cable plants already at peak capacity.
Electron beam solar wire facility started at Sanand; management expects solar wire contribution to grow quarter on quarter from a small FY26 base at similar margins.
Planned backward integration: medium-voltage XLPE compound manufacturing (at least 2 years away); considering captive galvanised steel armour wire given about 5,000 tonnes per month consumption.
Unused QIP proceeds of about INR385 crores expected to be deployed in FY27 with Sanand phase 2.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as strong across power T&D, data centres, metro rail and railways, commercial construction, and oil and gas; thermal and renewable power generation seen as growth drivers.
Pricing is pass-through on an order-by-order basis for tender-driven institutional business; retail prices revised twice a month. Average copper price rose 16.85% and aluminium 9.91% in FY26.

Order book at 31 March 2026 about INR3,585 crores: domestic institutional cables INR2,154 crores, export cables INR497 crores, EHV power cables INR625 crores, EPC INR309 crores; further EHV L1 orders of INR233 crores.

Middle East shipments were disrupted in March (no shipping lines); April resumed via Fujairah at high cost, with customers bearing about 50% of the extra freight. Imports of XLPE from Abu Dhabi were disrupted, but no plant has suffered raw-material shortage.
Receivables from the B2C business are falling as channel financing is used; the working capital cycle is expected to decline.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue growth likely to reach 25-30% given volume growth and copper prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this could happen if metal prices hold, but gave no firm value-growth target; Rajeev said value growth will exceed 20% at current prices.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the quarter's margin expansion despite freight and Middle East issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East freight costs hit April, not March, and that extra freight would be offset by favourable exchange rates on orders priced at about INR90-91 per dollar.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 volume growth only about 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev said it was mainly capacity constraints, with Sanand Q4 sales under INR100 crores as ramp-up is slow; he expects 17-18% volume growth from FY27 as Sanand is now operational.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of INR600-700 crores a year for 2-3 years, funded from internal accruals (60-70% capex, 30-40% working capital); no borrowing planned.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the remaining net cash will be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev said INR500-600 crores of cash will be held at all times for operations; the balance above that can fluctuate with working capital needs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US export opportunity and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US sales restarted after tariff relief, with the US order book at about INR50-60 crores; average export EBITDA margin is about 11%. Data-centre supply is mainly medium-voltage HT cables.

risks_watch: Sanand phase 2 delays: management already pushed the schedule by 6 months once, and phase 2 is now due by March 2027.
Middle East shipping and freight disruption; April freight costs are partly absorbed by KEI, and about INR50-60 crores of March exports were lost.
Volume growth was weak in FY26 (6.21%) and Q4 (about 2%); the 17-18% FY27 guidance depends on Sanand ramp-up.
Dependence on imported EHV XLPE compounds and continued supply of imported XLPE from Abu Dhabi.
Competition in US data-centre cables from domestic US manufacturers; US tariff exposure.
Receivables and inventory trends; management said Q4 acceptance and trade payables are elevated due to higher metal prices.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FY27 volume plan, but noticeably hedged on value growth and margins ("could happen", "conservative" 10.5-11% margin guidance). Some answers on volumes and capital allocation were vague or contradictory, and the call had a few clarifications on figures.
key_quotes: We are expecting 17% to 18% volume growth in this current financial year, which will mainly coming from Sanand new facility.
I mean on a conservative side, we can now expect around 11% -- anywhere between 10.5% to 11%.
Rajeev Gupta: Yes, it was mainly because of the capacity constraint actually.
Because we are running a debt-free company. And with this guidance, we will be continuing running as a debt-free company for next 4 to 5 years.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 volume growth of 17-18% (value growth above 20% at current metal prices), mainly from the Sanand phase 2 facility, which is now expected by March 2027, backed by a INR3,585 crore order book at 31 March 2026 but without a detailed phase-2 capacity figure.
